default.rationale: SM6 admits seven predictors equally - BayesDel, MutPred2, REVEL and VEST4 from ClinGen's first evaluation (PMID 36413997), AlphaMissense, ESM1b and VARITY_R from its second (PMID 40084623) - so being on that list is this entry's precondition, not its reason. The reason is measured performance on curated clinical variants: in a diagnostic laboratory's comparison of five of them - BayesDel, REVEL, VARITY_R, AlphaMissense and MutPred2 - over its own missense variants submitted to ClinVar, judged against its internal classifications, BayesDel ranked ahead of the other four overall, and the comparison notes BayesDel, REVEL and VARITY_R are already among the tools the ACMG v4 draft recommends. The lead is not uniform: BayesDel ranks first on the pathogenic side but behind VARITY_R on the benign side. Two bounds on how far the ranking generalises: it rests on one laboratory's classifications, and on thresholds that laboratory selected as most applicable to its own practice (citing the same two ClinGen evaluations), not on the SM6 Figure 2 bins this library scores with. The comparison is unpublished, so this entry cites its ranking and not its accuracy figures, which are the authors' to publish. The flavour is forced rather than preferred - ClinGen calibrated the no-allele-frequency build, which is why SM6 Figure 2 labels the row bare 'BayesDel', and there is no GRCh38 build of addAF at all.
default.source: SM6 (Missense Variants): the approved-predictor paragraph and the Figure 2 threshold table. Ciotta C, De Fazio P, Lunke S, Stark Z, 'A comparative analysis of in silico tool performance on manually curated missense variants: single laboratory experience' - Victorian Clinical Genetics Services / Murdoch Children's Research Institute / University of Melbourne. Conference poster, unpublished; no DOI or PMID sighted.

genes.rationale: Two findings, from two sources; neither alone would carry the entry. First, the default is specifically weak on this gene: of the five tools compared over one laboratory's curated set, BayesDel ranks last on the PKD1 pathogenic-prediction rate, below AlphaMissense. Second, on a PKD1 truth set re-classified under ACMG/AMP from ClinVar and PKDB reports, AlphaMissense was the only one of five tools - SIFT, PolyPhen-2, CADD, REVEL, AlphaMissense - to misclassify no truth-set variant. The three tools ranking above AlphaMissense on that rate are not selected: MutPred2 ranks last of the five on benign / likely-benign calls across the whole curated set, so a positive call from it carries little information; REVEL is in the preprint's five as well, so the second finding is a gene-specific result against it - it misclassified truth-set variants and AlphaMissense did not; and neither source reports a specificity result for VARITY_R on this gene. What neither source shows is that AlphaMissense is good on PKD1 - only that it is less bad than the default, and that its errors are omissions rather than wrong calls: many PKD1 scores fall between its pathogenic and benign thresholds, and BayesDel was absent from the medRxiv comparison, so the two are never measured head to head on one truth set. Both sources describe the gene rather than the tool - every tool in the laboratory's comparison did significantly worse on PKD1 than over its full dataset, and no genome-wide threshold separates pathogenic from benign PKD1 missense reliably - and the laboratory's own recommendation is that groups analysing PKD1 calibrate gene-specific thresholds rather than substitute tools. This entry is the interim answer until such a calibration exists. The per-gene rates behind it are unpublished and the authors' to publish, so this entry cites the ranking only.
genes.source: Ciotta C, De Fazio P, Lunke S, Stark Z, 'A comparative analysis of in silico tool performance on manually curated missense variants: single laboratory experience' - Victorian Clinical Genetics Services / Murdoch Children's Research Institute / University of Melbourne. Conference poster, unpublished; no DOI or PMID sighted. And: 'Challenges in Classification of PKD1 Missense Variation in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease', medRxiv 2026: https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.07.30.26359376v1
